title: The Great Big Yarn of Mel's Hole
summary: Josh and Chuck dig into "Mel's Hole," a bizarre tale first told on Art Bell's Coast to Coast AM in the late 1990s by a caller named Mel Waters from Ellensburg, Washington. Mel describes a bottomless hole on his property with a black beam, silent gunshots, a time-travel radio-producing WWII pistol, impossible 1943 Roosevelt dimes, a second "Basque hole," and a fetal seal with human eyes. The hosts walk through the story's claims, the 2002 expedition led by Gerald Osborne (Red Elk), the skeptical geologist Jack Powell, and the later internet myths, and conclude it is best treated as radio theater. Mel Waters appears not to exist, according to the hosts. The episode closes with a listener mail about the Mong people and the Secret War in Laos.
topics: Northwest Museum of Legends and Lore

entities.name: Northwest Museum of Legends and Lore

segments.title: Opening and Coast to Coast AM background
segments.summary: The hosts set up the episode as a tall tale and describe Art Bell's Coast to Coast AM, its fax-in format, and George Noory's later takeover.

segments.title: Introducing Mel's Hole
segments.summary: Mel Waters describes a nine-foot-wide stone-lined hole on his property near Ellensburg, Washington, with a barrier wall and no discernible bottom.

segments.title: Strange properties: black beam and silent echo
segments.summary: Mel reports that dumped trash never fills the hole, no sound comes back, and a neighbor saw a black beam shoot skyward. A Stonehenge comparison from a neighbor is also discussed.

segments.title: The silent WWII gun that picks up time-travel radio
segments.summary: Mel finds a World War Two Walther P38 that fires silently and, when placed near a radio, pulls in broadcasts from different times.

segments.title: Skepticism about Art Bell and the hoax question
segments.summary: The hosts debate whether Art Bell could have staged the story and whether the dog-resurrection claim and Mel's will to be thrown in the hole are credible.

segments.title: Dog resurrection and transition
segments.summary: A neighbor's claim that a dog thrown into the hole returned alive is recounted, along with Art Bell's suggestion about terminal patients.

segments.title: Break and pun
segments.summary: Short break with a pun on Stucks.

segments.title: Depth test with shark reel and Lifesavers
segments.summary: Mel uses shark fishing reels and a weighted line to measure depth, first with a roll of Lifesavers, then with line reaching roughly 80,000 feet. Callers suggest university help and compare the depth to the Mariana Trench and the Kola borehole.

segments.title: Government blockade and Terra Server
segments.summary: Mel is blocked from his land by military personnel and a man in a suit who threatens a drug-lab frame. Mel finds his property missing from Terra Server, and the hosts mention the nearby military installation and NSA listening station.

segments.title: Fiber optic cable, Livermore instruments, and the land lease
segments.summary: A trucker friend reports delivering fiber optic cable and Lawrence Livermore Laboratory instruments to an Ellensburg warehouse. Mel's land is then leased anonymously for a quarter million dollars a month.

segments.title: Move to Australia and the security deposit gun
segments.summary: Mel says he moved to Australia, where he grows medicinal herbs and rescues wombats, and used the gun as a security deposit. The hosts note Australian entry is hard.

segments.title: Mel's assault, missing teeth, and impossible 1943 dimes
segments.summary: Mel reports waking up in San Francisco missing his ID, belt buckle, and back teeth. His buckle held a 1943 Roosevelt dime that does not exist. The Treasury Department reportedly confiscated one from a coin dealer.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Break with another Stucks pun.

segments.title: The Basque hole and the eternal hot ice
segments.summary: Mel learns of a second hole, the Basque hole, with a metal collar that stays warm and a block of ice that does not melt and later catches fire. A Basque man's wood stove and cabin collapse into dust.

segments.title: Sheep experiment and the tumor seal
segments.summary: A sheep is lowered into the Basque hole and returns dead. A tumor inside it contains a fetal seal with human eyes that later heals Mel's cancer, which the hosts describe as internet-grown folklore.

segments.title: Hoax indicators and the local rumor
segments.summary: No record of Mel Waters or his wife's job at Central Washington University exists, suggesting a local hoax. A real local superstition about a bottomless hole is noted.

segments.title: 2002 expedition, Red Elk, and Jack Powell's skepticism
segments.summary: A 2002 expedition led in part by Gerald Osborne (Red Elk) searches for the hole. Geologist Jack Powell says the hole is impossible. The group forms the Seattle Paranormal Society, and the Northwest Museum of Legends and Lore tracks updates until about 2003.
topics: Northwest Museum of Legends and Lore

segments.title: Internet afterlife and the Musk drone myth
segments.summary: Online retellings grow dumber, including a Lazarus pit reference and a YouTube video claiming a drone sent by Elon Musk found something at the bottom. The hosts conclude the story works best as radio theater.

segments.title: Transition to listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts agree the story is theater and transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail on the Secret War and Hmong people
segments.summary: Melody writes asking for an episode on the Hmong people recruited in the Secret War in Laos, following up on the Project 100,000 episode. The hosts say it could deserve its own episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address and iHeartRadio credits.
